criteria.note: warp_streaming_runner.py ships at plugin/templates/scripts/runners/streaming/. run(journey, source) reads name, optional sequence_field, ordered expected_events, required terminal matcher, optional final graders with assemble_field, and a fake frame list; the SOURCE seam is a callable defaulting to journey fake frames (verified source=lambda works, no live server). parse_sse_frame genuinely parses SSE: field: value lines with one leading space stripped, comment (colon-prefixed) lines ignored, required data field, colon-less line and unknown field are framing errors. main() exits 0 when all assertions hold, exits 1 naming the first failure. Reran test_streaming_runner.sh: well-formed exit 0, malformed exit 1, rc 0.

I independently tampered the well-formed fixture three ways against a fresh import. DROP (i=0,1,3): fails 'sequence i: frame 2 expected index 2, got 3'. DUPLICATE (i=0,1,1,2): fails 'sequence i: frame 2 expected index 2, got 1'. REORDER (i=1,0,2 and i=2,0,1): fails 'sequence i: frame 0 expected index 0, got 1/2'. Contiguous-increasing-from-0 in arrival order is genuinely enforced (expected counter incremented only on match, terminal frames skipped, break on first gap), not faked. expected_events is matched one to one with length check plus first positional mismatch named.

Framing enforced: colon-less line, unknown field, and data-less frame each return framing errors naming the index/content (verified). Terminal required and must be last: missing terminal fails 'stream did not terminate'; a single frame after the terminal fails 'frame arrived after the terminal'. Final graders (contains/not_contains/equals/regex) run over concatenated NON-terminal frame data only (verified terminal data excluded from assembly). asserts-nothing journey (no sequence_field/expected_events/terminal/final) is a journey error, does not rubber-stamp. See note finding re: a duplicated-terminal-with-trailing-content edge.

The streaming block (lines 1190-1254) exercises all control logic with a fake in-memory source and no network/external dependency: happy stream, parse_sse_frame valid/colon-less/data-less/unknown-field, sequence gap, reorder, malformed-frame-in-stream, missing terminal, frame-after-terminal, failed final grader, asserts-nothing, wrong-event-type, source-seam, and both shipped fixtures driven end to end (pass exit 0, dropped chunk exit 1 naming the gap). All prior cases still pass.

Case-insensitive scan of the runner, fixtures, wrapper, and README for company/product names (bcengi, dejitech, travelpass, workpass, agentpass, coreconnect, onesim, mvne, dmitry, grinberg, stripe, hubspot, webflow, instantly, scraper) returned zero matches. .warp/capabilities.yaml declares streaming_sse_runner status: reference (never mechanical) and is byte-identical to plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml (sha256 7d078bbe..., diff empty). ./scripts/verify.sh is GATE: GREEN at 119fe7c, 0 undeclared. No em/en dash in any added file; only ASCII `--` is the `# ---` selftest section divider, the file's pervasive 26-use convention, not gate-flagged.

findings.text: Terminal check keys on the LAST matching terminal frame (term_idx[-1]). A stream of the shape [terminal, non-terminal, terminal] (e.g. done, token, done) passes when the journey asserts terminal ONLY, because a terminal is present as the final frame. This means a frame arriving after an EARLIER terminal is not caught in that narrow case. Not blocking: (a) the standard defect - a single terminal followed by trailing content - IS caught; (b) any journey that also declares expected_events catches it via the count/order mismatch (verified: the double-terminal case fails when expected_events is set); (c) it requires the terminal event type to recur, an atypical malformation. The documented semantics ('terminal must be the LAST frame') are internally consistent with the implementation.

The added selftest streaming block header uses '# ---' (an ASCII double-hyphen). This is a code comment section divider, matches the file's established convention (26 '# ---' dividers, one per runner block), is not prose or outbound copy, and is not flagged by the repo's own dash sweep (scripts/check_docs.sh forbids only em-dash U+2014 and en-dash U+2013). No em/en dash and no other '--' appear in any added file.

summary: Reran everything rather than trusting the manifest: test_streaming_runner.sh (well-formed exit 0 / malformed exit 1, rc 0), selftest.py (345 passed, 0 failed), verify.sh (GATE GREEN at 119fe7c). Independently tampered the well-formed fixture three ways and confirmed a dropped, a duplicated, and a reordered chunk each FAIL naming expected vs got; contiguous-from-0 is genuinely enforced. Framing (colon-less, unknown field, data-less), a missing terminal, a single frame-after-terminal, failed final graders over non-terminal data, and an asserts-nothing journey all fail loud - no rubber-stamp. Runner is generic (zero names), capabilities marks it status: reference and is byte-identical across .warp and plugin/templates. Recomputed proof_digest = sha256:0cb11f90bb7ffd79, matches. One narrow non-blocking note: a duplicated-terminal-with-trailing-content stream passes under a terminal-only journey (caught in practice by expected_events). Verdict: pass.
